document.title: Succinct Interactive Oracle Proofs: Applications and Limitations

candidate.title: Circuit Satisfiability Resists Small Space with Preprocessing
candidate.subtitle: A space-time hypothesis whose consequence is a limitation on succinct interactive oracle proofs
candidate.one_line: CSAT for size-n circuits over m inputs cannot be solved in poly(m) space with t(n,m)-time probabilistic preprocessing, for t in a given class T.
candidate.status_note: Conjecture 1.2 of the source, a parameterized family rather than a single claim. Corollary 1.3 turns each parameter setting into a limitation on succinct IOPs. The source attaches decreasing confidence as the class T grows, calling the largest setting only '(arguably) unlikely' to be false.
candidate.progress_note: Calibration in the source's Appendix A: CVAL is P-complete under log-space reductions, but the best known algorithm is the pebbling approach at O(n/log n) space, and pebbling provably cannot do much better. Since m can be far below n, poly(m) space is a different regime.

parameters.meaning: circuit size and number of input bits; the regime of interest has m much less than n
the class of preprocessing-time bounds t(n,m); larger T gives a stronger conjecture and a stronger IOP bound

candidate.why_interesting: It converts a question about the limits of succinct IOPs into a space-time question about circuit satisfiability, and the source shows any refutation must itself be a genuine space-time result.
candidate.why_clean: Two counted resources, one problem, one function class parameterizing the whole family.

quotes.quote: For a function class T , the conjecture states that CSAT for circuits of size n over m input bits cannot be solved by an algorithm that uses poly(m) space and t(n, m)-time probabilistic preprocessing, for any t ∈ T .
we conjecture that even probabilistic quasi-polynomial time preprocessing would not be sufficient, and taking things
With t(n, m) = poly(n), there is no succinct IOP for RCSAT with a constant number of rounds and O(log n) query complexity.
it would imply a surprising interplay between space and time complexities and in particular, yield an interesting space-time trade-off for CSAT.
it was later proved that for general circuits, the pebbling approach cannot do much better

check.notes: Conjecture 1.2 is verbatim on page 5 and is transcribed as printed, including its parameterization by T. The correction is one of emphasis, recorded in a dedicated remark: because the conjecture is a scale of hypotheses rather than one claim, and because the source explicitly attaches different confidence to different settings of T, a resolution in either direction is meaningless unless it names its T. Without that remark a reader would take the statement to be a single proposition.
